# Package `thaumcraft.api.nodes`

[All packages](README.md)

## INode

```java
public interface INode extends IAspectContainer
```

The original TC4 node contract.

Forced 1.21.1 change: none of the members changed; the essence amount of the original was a `short` and stays one.

**The identity of the node.** Oracle `thaumcraft/api/nodes/INode.java:12-29` publishes `getId()`, and the original node derived that identity from its own position (`dim:x:y:z`, oracle `thaumcraft/common/tiles/TileNode.java:98-115`). The native node keeps a **persisted random UUID** instead, and that UUID is the identity the scan of the node uses (the phenomena key `NODE<uuid>`). The format cannot be changed without invalidating the accepted client evidence of the port: the client test `fabric/src/clientTest/java/thaumcraft/fabric/clienttest/FocalManipulatorClientSequence.java:509` parses the identity with `UUID.fromString`, the accepted saved worlds carry the UUIDs in their node NBT and the accepted scan records carry the phenomena string `@NODE1b1965a9-747f-4d43-82ff-91e1f0ab443b` (`fabric/src/clientTest/java/thaumcraft/fabric/clienttest/BoreClientSequence.java:870-871`). Every other member of the contract carries the original's semantics exactly.

**The aspect lists are copies.** The original returned its live `AspectList` from `getAspects()` and `getAspectsBase()`; the native returns a copy, so an add-on can never mutate the state of a node through the published view. The values are the original's.

<a id="inode-getid"></a>
```java
String getId()
```

The identity of the node.

Original `INode:14`: the identity the original derived from the position of the node (`dim:x:y:z`, oracle `TileNode:98-115`). The native node returns its persisted UUID instead; see the javadoc of this interface for why that format is kept.

<a id="inode-getaspectsbase"></a>
```java
AspectList getAspectsBase()
```

The base of the node: the capacity of every aspect of the node.

Original `INode:16` and `TileNode:190,265-271`: the base is the amount the node may hold of an aspect, and writing it changes **only** the base, never the current essence of the node.


## NodeAdapter

```java
public class NodeAdapter implements INode
```

The public view of the native aura node.

The original TC4 node itself implements the published contract (oracle `thaumcraft/common/tiles/TileNode.java:75-77`), so an add-on casts the block entity of a node to `INode`. The native node does the same: it implements `INode` with the published `NodeType` and `NodeModifier` enums, exactly as the original published them. This adapter stays as the documented bridge for an add-on that holds a reference to the native node and wants the published view of it; both views share the same state, the same write path and the same identity.

Forced 1.21.1 change: none of the members changed; the native node carries the published enums, so no translation by name is needed any more.

```java
public NodeAdapter(TileNode node)
```

## NodeBase

```java
public class NodeBase implements INode
```

A complete, self-contained `INode` implementation for an add-on's own node.

The native aura node is the game's own node; an add-on that contributes a node type implements this class instead of the native one. Current stock and base capacity are separate: lowering the base through `setNodeVisBase` does not reduce current essence and can leave stock above capacity.

```java

public AspectList getAspects()

public NodeType getNodeType()

public void setNodeModifier(NodeModifier nodeModifier)

```

<a id="nodebase-doescontaineraccept"></a>


Always true, even for null: this is a capability answer, not validation that an insertion will succeed.


Null aspects or nonpositive amounts return the full amount unchanged; other insertions return the unaccepted remainder.

<a id="nodebase-takefromcontainer"></a>


Returns false for null aspects, nonpositive amounts or insufficient contents without removing anything.
